publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a method that combines the microwave network theory with MoM-FDTD algorithm to calculate the isolation between antennas involving dielectric objects is presented. First, a novel iteration procedure of a hybrid method combining the method of moments with the finite-difference time-domain method is employed to simulate the antennas with dielectric objects. Then, the network theory is introduced to calculate the mutual impedance and the isolation between antennas involving dielectric bodies. Numerical results validate the accuracy and efficiency of the analytic method presented here for EMC

articleTitle: Broadband slot antenna with a fan-shaped microstrip feed
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel slot antenna with a large bandwidth and small size is introduced, which is fed by a fan-shaped microstrip feed with a straight stub. The effect of the fan feed on the impedance characteristics is investigated theoretically and experimentally. Good agreement between theoretical results and experimental ones is obtained. Its measured VSWR /spl les/ 2 bandwidth reaches approximately 114%, covering 1.55 GHz - 5.66 GHz . The measured standing-wave ratio curves and radiation patterns of the antenna at f = 2 GHz and at f = 5 GHz both are presented.

articleTitle: A multiple-cores shared-tree multicast routing algorithm for LEO satellite IP networks
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new multicast routing algorithm, namely multiple-cores shared-tree (MCST), is proposed especially for low earth orbit (LEO) satellite IP networks. MCST can create a shared tree with multiple cores for each dynamic multicast group. And the outward extending searching square (OESS) approach is developed to select cores for multicast groups in the network, also core updating and dynamic management of group membership are supported in the algorithm. Simulation results show that MCST has good tree cost performance. In addition, MCST not only can balance traffic in the network, but it is robust by using multiple cores.

articleTitle: A new predistorter based on memory polynomials and LUT
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Digital base band predistortion is a highly cost-effective way to linearize PAs, but the existing architectures assume that the PA has a memory less nonlinearity. For wideband application, such as DVB-T (digital video broadcasting-terrestrial) system, PA memory effects can no longer be ignored. The predistorter based on look-up table (LUT) cannot compensate the distortion caused by memory effects. The predistorter based on memory polynomials (MPM) is an effective approach for the linearization of PAs with memory effects. But when the nonlinearly of PAs becomes stronger, the performance of MPM becomes worse. In this paper, we give the simulation results of the predistortion based on MPM with DVB-T signal, and analyze the drawback of the approach. At the end of the paper, we proposed a new predistorter based on both memory polynomial and LUT. It is implemented using an indirect learning architecture.

articleTitle: Cross-talk interference aggressor signal frequency estimation in printed circuit boards by means of wavelet signal singularity identification
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for cross-talk interference aggressor signal frequency estimation in a PCB by means of Wavelet signal singularity identification, to assist PCB designers tracing the aggressor signal according to its frequency character. Wavelet signal singularity is employed to identify the rise and fall sides of the aggressor pulse from the disturbed (victim) signal. The rise and fall sides of the aggressor pulse are then directly processed to determine the frequency of the aggressor signal that characterizes the disturbance signal, and may lead to the identification of the source of aggressor signal.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of digital watermarking through OFDM channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Different most used image watermarking scheme performances while transmitted over OFDM multi-path channels both with Doppler shift and without Doppler shift have been evaluated. Simulation results have shown that the system suffers from the Doppler shift and the watermarking performances are also decreased while the Doppler shift increasing.

articleTitle: New improved macromodelings for on-chip RLC interconnects
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Two kinds of new improved macromodelings are proposed for on-chip RLC interconnects. By applying the global approximations, the equivalent circuits of on-chip RLC interconnects are derived, which are presented by the improved T model and /spl Pi/ model. Also, by applying the method asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE), the other kind of new improved T model and /spl Pi/ model can be obtained. The result of examples shows that all these models reach a good accuracy and can work much faster than SPICE. Furthermore, it can be incorporated into SPICE frames easily.

articleTitle: A new receiver architecture for smart antenna with digital beamforming
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Smart antennas are regarded as the key solution to increasing the spectral efficiency and improving the system performance in wireless communications. The high speed analog to digital converter (ADC) and digital signal processor (DSP) make the smart antenna with digital beamforming (DBF) a reality. In conventional N-element array receiving system, each element has its own RF/IF channel and ADC. In this paper, a novel smart antenna receiver with digital beamforming is proposed The essential idea is to realize the digital beamforming receiver based on bandpass sampling of multiple IF signals. The proposed system reduced receiver hardware from N IF channels and N ADCs to one IF channel and one ADC using a heterodyne RF circuitry and a multiple bandpass sampling receiver. In this scheme, the sampling rate of the ADC is much higher than the summation of the N times of the signal bandwidth. The local oscillator produces different local frequency for each RF channel. The receiver architecture is presented and the simulation of bandpass sampling of multiple signals is given.

articleTitle: Space-time code in cooperative diversity wireless network
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the idea of space-time coding proposed for multiple-antenna system is applied to cooperative diversity wireless network. The pair error probability of the proposed scheme is analyzed and compared with the multiple antenna system. In the condition that the total transmit power is constant, the several power allocation schemes between the source and the relay nodes are given. The result indicates that wireless networks with R cooperative partners can achieve the same diversity as multiple antenna systems with R transmit antennas at asymptotically high transmit power when space-time codes are used distributive among the R cooperative partners.

articleTitle: Study on effect experiment of ESD EMP to single chip microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Choosing 8031 minimal systems, a familiar MCS-51 series SCM (single chip microcontroller), as experimental object, this-paper studies irradiation field effects & effecting mechanism of ESD EMP (electrostatic discharge electromagnetic pulse) via effecting experiment and theory research respectively. The interference & damage threshold of SCM in different, failure modes are ascertained. By analyzing the failure reasons, some rules of ESD EMP effects are concluded. This paper serves to provide practical SCM designs with a thorough and heady reference in dealing with complex-ESD protection design for automatic control equipment

articleTitle: Visual discrete GTD ray path tracing on aircraft
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The problem of visual discrete GTD (geometrical theory of diffraction) ray path tracing on aircraft is investigated. Quickly-3D-model for electronic countermeasures aircrafts is carried out based on OpenGL. The model provides surface discrete grids data. Enough points can be achieved by minutely modeling or interpolating splines and nodes. According to Fermat principle, the length of geodesic path is calculated with the method of dynamic programming on the platform surface discrete grids served as. Visual discrete GTD ray path tracing on aircraft is realized with the method of recursive dynamic programming. This work provides an approach for quickly analyzing antenna isolation degree on early warning aircrafts, strategic reconnaissance aircrafts and electronic support aircrafts

articleTitle: Application of cryogenic tuning technique in an HTS filter
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes a method for tuning an HTS filter at the cryogenic temperature. Sonnet software was used for simulating the distribution of current density. Dielectric tuning screws were used to regulate the redistribution of electromagnetic field, so that the response characteristics of the filter can be improved. For matching the designed result, this technique allows correcting the deviation caused by fabrication processing and non uniformity of substrate thickness and dielectric constant. 9-pole forward-coupling microstrip filter as a sample shows its response characteristics before and after tuning. The tuning result showed better performance than simulation. The insertion loss and return loss were improved and the center frequency shift towards the low end after tuning

articleTitle: Computationally efficient antenna selection in MISO-STBC-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In the downlink of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) from the base station to the mobile receiver, in order to reduce the receiver decoding; complexity, capture the benefits of a multiple transmit antenna system while at the same time exploit the diversity gain provided by space-time block coding (STBC), we consider transmit antenna selection in an MISO-STBC-OFDM system. To find the optimal pair of antennas in an MISO-STBC-OFDM system, a computational-intensive exhaustive search is usually required. In this paper, we propose an antenna selection method with reduced complexity, based on the norm of the channel impulse responses in the time domain. This proposed antenna selection method exhibits near-optimal bit-rate, bit-error rate (BER) and outage probability performances as substantiated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Accurate geometrical analysis of sector dwell time distribution
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present accurate evaluation of sector dwell time distribution based on geometric analysis methods. Considering the nature geometric characteristic of the deployed sector pattern, and the distribution of the mobiles' position and moving direction in the given sector, we derive the accurate formulas of the probability density function of sector cell dwell time. Some numerical results are also presented for illustration

articleTitle: Study on the verification standard of electrostatic discharge generators (acc. IEC 61000-4-2)
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Through systemic study on two types of electrostatic discharge (ESD), generators and the effects of discharge switch to ESD immunity test; it has been found that the verification of ESD generators presents a number of problems. The experimental results show that ESD generators from different manufactures yield different results while testing products, even if the discharge currents are quite similar. This means that it is incomplete that the IEC 61000-4-2 only specifies the values of the characteristics of the discharge current of the ESD generator during the verification procedure. To resolve this problem, besides ESD current waveform, the IEC 61000-4-2 standard should specify discharge current derivative, transient field, and induced voltages in detail.

articleTitle: Uplink performance of complex wavelet packet based multi-carrier CDMA system with space diversity combining technique
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, based on the analysis of the principle of multi-carrier code division multiple access (MC-CDMA) and the use of the optimized complex wavelet packet, a complex wavelet packet based MC-CDMA (CWP-MC-CDMA) system uplink model is proposed, and space diversity combining (SDC) technique is adopted to perfect the system performance. Meanwhile, the ICWPT (inverse complex wavelet packet transform)/CWPT replaces IDFT/DFT operator in conventional MC-CDMA for multi-carrier modulation and demodulation, thus the decrease of spectrum efficiency of conventional MC-CDMA due to inserting cyclic prefix is overcome by utilizing the superior properties of optimized complex wavelet packet. The uplink performance of the proposed CWP-MC-CDMA system with SDC technique is investigated in Rayleigh fading channel, and corresponding BER (bit error rate) analysis is also given in detail. The theoretical analysis and simulation result show that the application of space diversity combining technique can improves the proposed CWP-MC-CDMA system ability to combat spatial fading and various interferences effectively. Moreover, the proposed system based on SDC technique has superior BER performance over the DFT and SDC based MC-CDMA system and real wavelet packet and SDC based MC-CDMA system.

articleTitle: A nonlinear servo control method base on integral backstepping scheme
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: For mechanical servo system, a novel servo controller based on integral backstepping scheme is presented, the controller has strong robustness to external disturbance and system parameter changes. Simulation results for a DC motor servo system show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: The study of fuzzy neural networks in train section following space interval model under MAS
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Train tracing space interval model system is the base of train dynamic run space control system. Owing to the uncertainly factors in the train run process, the math model based on draught account is difficult to satisfy the need of the practical system. Combining the characteristics of train dynamic run in MAS, this paper proposes a new train section tracing space interval model-based on neural networks and fuzzy control, whose name is the multi-input fuzzy neural network model. At last the paper point out its practical meaning and also proves the designed system's practicability by the simulation.

articleTitle: A 2.45 GHz wide tuning range VCO using MOS varactor in 0.35 /spl mu/m SiGe BiCMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A full monolithic low-phase-noise wide-tuning-range voltage-control-oscillator (VCO) designed for a dual-band homodyne transceiver for WLAN applications is presented in this paper. The circuit is designed and implemented in a commercial 0.35 SiGe BiCMOS process. MOS varactor is used to realize a wide tuning range. Measured VCO circuit specifications feature a 440 MHz tuning range around 2.45 GHz, phase noise of -110 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset and -106 dBc/Hz at 600 KHz, out power of 7.68 dBm and power dissipation of 6.8 mA with 3 V supplies.

articleTitle: Recent trend in technologies developments for wireless communications IEEE 2005 International Symposium on, Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE 2005)
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes on trend of the recent technology developments for wireless communications and consists of four parts. The first and most important development is the worldwide Internet traffic growth. The important trends in, the "worldwide Internet traffic" growth are summarized in terms of the global geographic areas and their Internet penetrations. The second item is the developments of the hardware supporting technologies for the backbone networks that are essential for the realization of wireless communications. The third item is the central issue for wireless communication, especially for local individual users. The fourth and last item is concluding remarks.

articleTitle: Distributed intelligent systems: what makes them "intelligent"
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Three core requirements are discussed for the implementation of distributed intelligent systems: a peer-to-peer communications infrastructure, a multi-agent architecture, and a means to provide distributed logistics for the management and self-organization of system resources. We distinguish between a distributed system and a distributed intelligent system, and the inherent advantages that they have over centralized methodologies. By incorporating intelligence in a distributed system, it is capable of cooperation, collaboration and coordination, features that have cardinal importance for highly configurable networks such as ad-hoc systems. We highlight research being conducted by Simon Fraser University and Intelligent Robotics Corporation to design and implement wireless distributed intelligent systems

articleTitle: Radiation from apertures on coaxial cables and conducting circular cylinders
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper reviews a Fourier transform and mode-matching analysis of radiation from apertures on coaxial cables and on conducting circular cylinders. The boundary-value problems of radiation from multiple apertures on conducting circular cylinders are solved subject to the boundary conditions. Analytic, rigorous solutions to the boundary-value problems are obtained using residue calculus. Salient features of Fourier transform and mode-matching techniques are discussed

articleTitle: Metamaterial properties, designs, and antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Metamaterials have the potential to allow engineers to tailor the electromagnetic responses of the materials incorporated in antenna systems to enhance their performance. Several examples of the exotic properties of electromagnetic metamaterials will be given. One class of metamaterials that has already demonstrated its usefulness with antennas is the artificial magnetic conductor (AMC). It has been demonstrated that this metamaterial configuration can yield a highly resonant radiating system. The resonances occur for particular combinations of shell sizes and metamaterial properties; they result in significant enhancements of the radiated power. These resonance results have been extended to lossy DNG and epsilon negative (ENG) metamaterials. We have also demonstrated reciprocity between these source results and the scattering of plane waves from the corresponding metamaterial coated spheres. We have shown with HFSS numerical simulations that realistic center-fed electrically small dipole antennas surrounded with an ENG spherical shell and coaxially-fed monopole antennas surrounded with an ENG hemispherical shell can be made to be resonant and matched to an external source. These electrically small antenna systems have very high radiation efficiencies and Q factors near the Chu limit. A review of these metamaterial-based electrically small antenna systems will be presented and current progress toward a proof-of-principle experiment will be discussed

articleTitle: A shortest path algorithm for mobile satellite communication network
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Mobile satellite network is a special time-varying network. Some classical network theories used in the current terrestrial networks, such as the shortest path algorithm, cannot be applied to it availably. In this paper, based on the proposed model of mobile satellite network, the classical shortest path algorithm of fixed topological network, such as the Dijkstra algorithm, is proved to be restrictive when it is applied in mobile satellite network. Here, a novel shortest path algorithm for mobile satellite network is given and optimized. Correlative simulation indicates that this algorithm can be effectively applied to the mobile satellite communication network.

articleTitle: Analysis of frequency diversity in MC-CDMA systems under correlated fading channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: MC-CDMA can obtain a good frequency diversity effect through spreading and despreading operation in frequency domain. In this paper, the impact of channel parameters to inherent frequency diversity is analyzed at first. Then, three spreading methods to achieve the frequency diversity are investigated. Not only frequency diversity but also multiple-user interference (MUI) is taken into account in our analysis. The achieved frequency diversity gains with different spreading methods are also affected by the combining schemes at the receivers when there are multiple users in the systems.

articleTitle: Phase noise mitigation for V-BLAST OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Future wireless mobile systems are required to transport multimedia traffics at much higher bit rates. Among all feasible implementations, V-BLAST OFDM system is one of the most promising candidates for such goal. However, similar to SISO-OFDM, V-BLAST OFDM suffers significant performance degradation due to the presence of phase noise. Although several phase noise mitigation method have been proposed in the literature for SISO channel, none has addressed this MIMO scenario, in which the performance degradation is more severe than SISO as it faces more complicated channel with little diversity gain. Moreover, in the original work of V-BLAST, a large number of antennas (8 transmit and 12 receive antennas) were proposed to obtain high bit rate. This may imply that multiple oscillators would be used to support such system. Most phase noise mitigation methods deal with one oscillator case, while in this paper, by considering the general case for any number of oscillators, we proposed a phase noise mitigation (PNM) scheme, which efficiently reduces the effect of multiple phase noise generated by different oscillators in V-BLAST OFDM system. Although the algorithm developed is based on independent MIMO channel, its effectiveness in correlated channel is also numerically evaluated.

articleTitle: New theory of isolation between antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In EMC study, the interaction of two-antenna system is usually described with isolation between antennas. In this paper, the authors point out the definition of traditional isolation between antennas is unreasonable and it will give incorrect isolation prediction. We put forward definitions of arbitrary isolation, ideal isolation and practical isolation of antennas according to three states of antenna system. With the definition of practical isolation, we can give the best and the worst values of isolation of the actual working antennas by only knowing the indexes of input and output VSWR.

articleTitle: Design of an electrical downtilt base station antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A base station antenna is an RF component capable of critically affecting performance of a cellular system. Most mobile subscribers are located in densely populated urban areas; frequency reuse is often implemented in system design. Downtilting base station antennas is used in mobile communication to prevent co-channel interference. Antenna downtilt is done mechanically or electrically. In electrical downtilt, excitation phases of elements are changed, and therefore the main lobe of the pattern is tilted. In this paper, we introduce antenna configuration for electrical downtilt. Here a genetically optimized technique is employed. Printed circuit dipoles are employed as radiation elements

articleTitle: Design problems for stepped-index Luneburg lens antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on a new method for the solution of the radiated fields of the stepped-index Luneburg lens antennas, the far field pattern as well as the gain of a stepped-index Luneburg lens antenna may be obtained in various situations. Examining these results, the answers to same problems related to manufacturing Luneburg lens may be obtained. For the more, needed information for feed design also can be obtained.

articleTitle: Modified generalized total-field/scattered-field FDTD boundary in PML region
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a modified generalized total-field/scattered-field (G-TF/SF) boundary for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) to model an infinite material scatterer within a compact FDTD grid when 0 /spl les/ /spl theta//sub inc/ /spl les/ 90/spl deg/ (/spl theta//sub inc/ is the wave propagation angle). This requires the sourcing of numerical plane wave traveling into the perfectly matched layer (PML) absorber bounding the grid. In this method, the modified G-TF/SF boundary can simplify the disposal of G-TF/SF boundary formulation. This technique is applied to model the electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and model 2-D TM diffraction of an infinite right-angle dielectric wedge. And there is a good correspondence between the results obtained by various methods.

articleTitle: Microwave characterization of carbonyl Fe/sub 55/Ni/sub 45/ fiber-filled composites
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Fiber-filled composites have the ability of tailoring the electric and magnetic properties and can be suitable for use as microwave lenses, high-strength low weight electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials, radar absorbing materials (RAM), antennas and waveguides, etc. The subject of this paper is to examine the microwave characterization of carbonyl Fe/sub 55/Ni/sub 45/ fiber-filled composites. With the method of the transmission and reflection waveguide, the complex permittivity and permeability of carbonyl Fe/sub 55/Ni/sub 45/ fiber-filled composites in S-band (2-4 GHz) were measured by a vector network analyzer. The reflection loss of these composites was also calculated in this frequency range. The results show that the strong skin effect can decrease the conductivity of fiber and ultimately reduce the effective permittivity of fiber-filled composites. The lower aspect ratio of carbonyl Fe/sub 55/Ni/sub 45/ fiber gives rise to the decrease of the effective magnetic field and the permeability. It was also found that the reflection loss of the composites is influenced more greatly by the low permittivity than that by thickness.

articleTitle: Dual-band microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop the microstrip patch designed for dual frequencies of 945 MHz and 1960 MHz. A new design of coplanar patches to get the dual band operation is proposed in this paper. It is a multiple patch approach for getting dual frequency operation with a single feed point. Some of the existing techniques like dual frequency PIFA; stacked patches for dual frequency and dual slot loaded patches are also designed for our specified frequency. Performance evaluation of all these design shows, our proposed design is advantageous in many aspects.

articleTitle: Element positioning applied to a low sidelobe level GSM base station array antenna design using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Element positioning is an effective approach in achieving low sidelobe level array antennas. In cases with few number of elements it becomes almost the best applicable solution. In this paper, the approach is applied to a 5times1 array antenna designed for GSM's BTS antenna application and the sidelobe reduction process and results are compared to that of phase only optimization. The sidelobe levels depend on element dimensions and the process highly clarifies the importance of element shrinking, which imposes a limit on the minimum possible sidelobe level. By considering element dimensions between lambda and 0.4 lambda, sidelobe levels ranging from -12.7 dB to -16.7 dB are derived using a genetic algorithm which could be quite satisfying for a 5-element equi-phase array

articleTitle: Coupling model for the two orthogonal microstrip lines in two layer PCB board (quasi-TEM approach)
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In the present paper a simple model has been given to simulate the signal propagation through two cross-orthogonal microstrip lines in two different layers of the PCB board. First, the structure has been analyzed using full wave software like HFSS, then a suitable lumped equivalent circuit is proposed for the cross talk region and its parameters are obtained. Finally, results of this equivalent circuit compared with results of full wave simulations that obtained from HFSS and microwave office software.

articleTitle: Wideband U-shaped cross section antenna with a strip on a U-shaped ground plane
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: By placing a U-shaped cross section antenna on a U-shaped ground plane, a U-shaped cross section antenna for wideband application is presented. The bottom of the U-shaped cross section antenna is etched to form a strip at the center and four arms. It can be extended the number of degree of freedom to match the impedance. Simulated results show that the impedance matching for the proposed antenna depends on the width of the center strip, the width of four arms and the height of the vertical sides of the U-shaped cross section antenna, and the impedance bandwidth is mainly determined by the width of the U-shaped ground plane. Simulated results of return loss and radiation patterns are also compared with the measured results after the antenna is fabricated. Both are in good agreement. The antenna has a measured impedance bandwidth of 29.17% (2:1 VSWR) of the frequency range 2.06-2.76 GHz and average gain level of 9.0/spl plusmn/0.5 dBi. Good radiation characteristics have been obtained that is, the front-to-back ratio is more than 15 dB across the bandwidth and the maximum cross polarization level is low at the high frequency.

articleTitle: Study on 2-D gyrotropic EBG by FEM
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the FEM of the hybrid of edge-element and node-element incorporated with Floquet theorem is employed for analyzing the electromagnetic characteristic of 2-D EBG consisting of gyrotropy medium. The method is certified by the comparison with analytic value. The required computational resources are small since the size of space domain to be solved is about only a single cell of the periodic structure. At the same time, the FEM of hybrid element satisfy the complexity of the electromagnetic field in the gyrotropy EBG. Then the analysis of ferrite EBG is presented, which shows the stop and pass bands are changed obviously by changing the biased magnetic filed. So the gyrotropy EBG (including ferrite EBG) probably became a novel tunable EBG. This paper is helpful for the design of this EBG.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of 2D RAC product codes in block coded modulation schemes
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A block coded modulation (BCM) scheme employing two-dimensional (2D) product codes, constructed from single parity check (SPC) sub-codes is described. A procedure for mapping encoded sequences to M-PSK signals and decoding using a compact trellis diagram are presented. Performance analysis parameters, such as information bit transmission rate, symbol rates, and coding gains are determined. It's shown that the proposed BCM technique can provide 2-3 dB coding gains.

articleTitle: Time-frequency RARE methods for direction finding
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method for the estimation of the DOA is introduced and named as TF-RARE method. The proposed method includes two steps. First, we construct time-frequency correlation matrix, then estimates DOA of the signals via RARE methods. The localization of the signals with different time-frequency signatures permits the division of the time-frequency domain into smaller regions. By using different time-frequency regions, the direction of the interested signals can be estimated. Simulations are presented to show the superior performance of the method.

articleTitle: Effect of element pattern on directivity of the hemispherical array
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In many communication scenarios, such as in GPS communications and integrated navigation systems, signals with wide space distributions need to be processed simultaneously or promptly. Hemispherical arrays have greater capability in receiving and processing signal than planar arrays, and can provide robust performance. In previous research, the directivity of a hemispherical array is compared with several kinds of planar arrays, that shows this kind of array has essentially better scanning performance. In this paper, the effect of element pattern on the hemispherical array's scanning directivity is studied, and the main factors which affect the parameters of directivity are analysed and the effects of these factors on directivity are discussed. Simulation results are presented for illustration.

articleTitle: Decoupled maximum likelihood detector of ST-FSK
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Combining the advantages of space-time block codes and frequency shift keying, space-time frequency shift keying (ST-FSK) can be ML detected noncoherently under the Rayleigh fading channels while providing full diversity. This paper presents a decoupled ML detection algorithm, which utilizes the orthogonal characteristic of signal. The proposed decoupled ML detector, under ideally known H and appropriate channel estimation, outperforms the noncoherent ML detector when the complexity is greatly reduced at the same time.

articleTitle: A novel method of planar near-field scattering measurements
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel method of planar near-field scattering measurements, i.e. the method of self-transmitting and self-receiving (STSR) planar near-field scattering measurements is studied in theory and validated experimentally. The experiment results show that the relative value of scattering property obtained by means of this method has good engineering precision in an angle range near the outward normal direction of the scanning plane, which proves the correctness, validity and engineering practicability of this method.

articleTitle: The research of an improved way of LHM realization-a renewed transmission line CRLH structure
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a renewed transmission line CRLH structure on the basis of former CRLH. A computed method is applied and this structure is found to be a RHM beneath a certain lower frequency while be an LHM above another certain higher frequency. Some other interesting phenomena occur in a special situation. With the help of some commercial computational and EM softwares, numerical and circuit simulations are used in order to verify our analysis result. The simulation results show that the renewed CRLH's topology is a typical duplexer topology which is identical with our analysis.

articleTitle: A blind source separation algorithm based on a unifying model
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a blind source separation algorithm, which can separate the mixture of super- and sub-Gaussian sources. A weighed tri-Gaussian model is proposed to estimate super- and sub-Gaussian probability density. The model can represent a broader range of sub-Gaussian densities as compared to some sub-Gaussian estimating models. In the framework of natural gradient, we derive the parameterized nonlinear score functions. Model parameters are calculated through online learning. Applying to the mixture of images, experiment shows that the proposed algorithm can efficient separate the mixture of super- and sub-Gaussian sources and has better performance

articleTitle: A solution for improving medium wave night broadcasting, using sky waves propagation
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The aim of this research is to provide a solution for better night propagation of medium wave (MW) broadcast transmitters through pattern change, type of applied propagation and without creating essential changes in transmitters. Important propagation problems of MW especially at the night are: (a) Co-channel interference of far transmitters at the night that (b) Decreases local coverage (LC) at night in comparison with day. (c) To cause problems for those transmitters being far coverage (FC) area and (d) Heavy traffic of MW band. Execution of proposed solution at this article causes economical savings and decreases number of transmitters as well as energy consumption. It also decreases field strength (FS) at the far area and the areas being out of LC and finally decreases undesirable interference

articleTitle: Two-dimensional time domain analysis of microstrip lines using RCMS model
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Two dimensional time domain analysis of microstrip transmission lines is presented. For this purpose, rigorously coupled multi-conductor strip (RCMS) model is used. In this model, the width of the strip of a microstrip line is subdivided into a large number of rigorously coupled narrow strips. Finally, some results are concluded for time domain behavior of microstrip transmission lines.

articleTitle: Study of planar near-field measurements methods for determining the gain of the antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The coupling equation and the formulas of the far-field pattern of the AUT determined from the near-field data in the case of considering all important proportional factors with the influence of the probe (i.e. the probe compensation) considered are given. Based on this, two methods for determining the gain of the antenna by means of planar near-field measurements, i.e. the absolute method and the comparative method are presented and the corresponding measurement principle and the calculation formulas are given

articleTitle: Self-structuring antenna for multi-band operation
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel antenna called self-structuring antenna (SSA) is proposed. The SSA has an advantage of altering its electrical shape in response to changing the states of switches, which makes it a multi-band antenna. The SSA comprised of rectangular ring antennas is designed by numerical electromagnetic code (NEC), and many numerical investigations are presented and shown that the proposed antenna can achieve multi-band operation.

articleTitle: Performance of multi-carrier CDMA system based on complex orthogonal wavelet packet in Nakagami-m fading channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on the analysis of the principle of multi-carrier CDMA and the use of optimized complex orthogonal wavelet packet, a complex orthogonal wavelet packet based MC-CDMA system (COWP-MC-CDMA) is proposed in this paper. We investigate the system downlink performance with EGC technique and MRC technique in Nakagami-m fading channels, respectively; and derive corresponding bit error rate (BER) expression in detail. The system may overcome the decrease of spectrum efficiency of DFT based conventional MC-CDMA (DFT-MC-CDMA) due to inserting cyclic prefix (CP). Theoretical analysis and simulation results show the COWP-MC-CDMA system outperforms DFT-MC-CDMA as well as real wavelet packet based MC-CDMA (RWP-MC-CDMA) system, it has superior ability to combat multi-path fading and multiaccess interference (MAI). Moreover, the BER performance of proposed system is slightly superior to that of the conventional MC-CDMA with CP.

articleTitle: Treatment of frequency-dependent underground cable using the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on the finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method, a new model is presented for the transient simulation of underground cable in this paper. For the convenience of the time-domain convolution, the vector fitting method (rational approximation in the frequency domain) is adopted to synthesize the skin effects of conductors and ground in the frequency domain. Thus, the problems associated with frequency-dependent transformation matrices are avoided. Additionally, the voltage and current wave processes on the underground cable can be obtained. Compared with other cable models, the new model proposed is demonstrated to be effective.

articleTitle: Phase matching technique for HTS filter-cryogenic LNA subsystem
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel kind of phase matching technique for improving the reflection loss performance of HTS filter subsystems is proposed. The basic principle is that excellent performance is obtained by realizing the inverse phase relationship of the HTS filter's S/sub 22/ parameter and the cryogenic LNA's S/sub 11/ parameter at those frequencies where poor S/sub 11/-peaks of the HTS filter exist. We applied this technique to an HTS filter subsystem for 800 MHz wireless communication. Simulation and test results are presented, and it has been proved that this technique is not only effective but also easy to apply and low cost.

articleTitle: Frequency offset estimation and compensation for downlink group-orthogonal multicarrier CDMA
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: We propose a carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation and compensation method for downlink group-orthogonal multicarrier code-division multiple-access (GO-MC-CDMA) system. The method exploits both the inherent orthogonality among subcarriers of different groups of GO-MC-CDMA system and the characteristics of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT ) demodulation. The CFO estimation is achieved by searching the value which minimizes the cost function constructed in terms of performing FFT on the interfering signals. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is very effective to estimate CFO of the downlink GO-MC-CDMA system. Besides, it is shown that after CFO compensation the bit error rate (BER) performance is improved significantly

articleTitle: Design of space-time trellis codes in fast and flat fading channel
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Improved design criteria for space-time trellis codes in fast fading channel are introduced and utilized. The criteria are based on union bound analysis and derived from the optimal FER performance. In the high SNR region the performance is governed primarily by symbol Hamming distance and the product criterion achieves an optimal coding gain, while in the low SNR region it is achieved by the trace criterion. We also discussed the performance behavior in the moderate SNR region. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed criteria are effective by comparing the performances of different codes.

articleTitle: A study on PML-FDTD and boundary consistency conditions of total-scattered fields in cylindrical coordinates
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain formula of Maxwell's equation in perfectly matched layer (PML-FDTD) is deduced in cylindrical coordinates. It is convenience to implement than in complex stretched coordinates that presented in Zhang Hongxin et al. (2002, 2003). Then, in order to study the scattering characteristics of cylindrical objects by using FDTD method, the boundary consistency conditions of total-scattered fields are proposed in cylindrical coordinates. Further, the planar wave excitation sources are set on the boundaries by using one dimension FDTD and linear interpolation method on attempt to simulate the propagation of plane (TEM) wave in free space. At last, the scattering patterns of a perfectly electric conductive cylinder are calculated in far zone, and the algorithm is validated by comparing with the results that of using the moment method (MoM).

articleTitle: Using non-uniform sampling to make automatic focusing result correct
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In automatic focusing system, the focusing window directly affects the speed and veracity of auto focusing. If focusing window is too big or too small, there will be incorrect focus result because of background in the window or object out of the window. A practical real-time auto-focus algorithm for digital camera is presented, and it improves the reliability and speed of auto focusing process. The proposed algorithm adopts non-uniform sampling and threshold gradient in order to get higher resolution in image central part and wider view field. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can be an effective alternative to most of the images, especially to the images in which the objects are out of focusing window or the objects don't content intensity changes in focusing window. In addition, the speed and veracity of focus are improved and the data of image is reduced.

articleTitle: Review of antennas designed for infrared detection a brief literature study
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper discusses how an antenna can be integrated with a detector for efficient and effective collection of THz radiations. Also, some results have been reproduced.

Author Keywords: double quantum well photo assisted tunneling

articleTitle: Several propagation properties of transient electromagnetic pulses
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Propagation properties of transient electromagnetic pulses, or ultra-wideband (UWB) pulses, are very important for UWB radio communication technology. General characteristics of UWB pulses are studied. The phase properties and the issues of waveform distortion are discussed further. Because of the complexity of phase properties of UWB signals, the analytic methods in time domain are preferred. The waveform distortion of UWB signals is caused by the frequency-selective fading when the antenna is included in the generalized channel. The transmitted waveform may be reconstructed through deconvolution method from the distorted waveform

articleTitle: Impact of PMD on the performance of NOLM and compensation by HN-FBG in microwave photonic systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The impact of the first-order and second-order PMD on the performance of NOLM is studied by the split-step Fourier method (SSFM) based on the coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equation (CNLSE), including sinusoidal modulation signals and power transmission function of NOLM with the first- and second-order PMD. Furthermore, the compensation method of PMD by the high-birefringence nonlinearly-chirped fiber Bragg grating (HN-FBG) in the middle of the fiber loop of NOLM is put forward.

articleTitle: Automated electromagnetic field measurements in urban environments
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Concentrating on the complex electromagnetic field in urban environments, the paper presents an automated system for electromagnetic field measurement covering the frequency of 9 kHz to 3 GHz. All the instruments in the system are connected to the host computer with GPIB, and they are controlled by software. In this system, the whole measurement procedure is operated automatically. The electromagnetic field can be measured each whole day, and the electromagnetic environment conditions can be reported to urban residents in time.

articleTitle: An approach to the dyadic Green's functions for a parallel-plate chirowaveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A method of the eigenfunction expansion of electromagnetic dyadic Green's functions in a parallel-plate chirowaveguide is given in this paper. By using this method, we can not only obtain the vector wave equations equivalent to that for chiral media but also similar to that for achiral media, the corresponding chiral eigenmodes in parallel-plate waveguides can take a similar form as the conventional achiral eigenmodes also, and then the dyadic Green's functions in a parallel-plate chirowaveguide can take a similar form as the conventional achiral dyadic Green's functions.

articleTitle: An adaptive hemispherical array
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Hemispherical arrays are charming in receiving and processing multiple signals with wide space distributions and thus provide robust performance for integrated navigation systems. Previous research [D. Li et al, 2005] shows this kind of array has better scanning directivity. In this paper, a geometry-optimized hemispherical array is studied on directivity and multiple signals/jammers adaptive processing. A practical switch network used to reduce activated elements number and thus cost is also proposed. Simulation examples are presented to illustrate its performance.

articleTitle: A differentiated path availability protection approach in WDM rings
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A differentiated path availability (DPA) protection approach in WDM ring networks was introduced. This approach can minimize the total wavelength mileage of ring, while guaranteeing the required path availability degree of each connection. The simulation result shows that in the uniform traffic study the used wavelength mileage decreases and the reused wavelength mileage increases, as the required availability degree of connection becomes lower. This rule fits in different traffic proportion scenarios.

articleTitle: High-isolation MEMS capacitive shunt switch
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Many efforts have been made to find materials with high dielectric constant for the application of RF capacitive shunt switch in order to obtain large down-state capacitance and therefore high isolation. In this work, HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> dielectric was suggested for the application of RF shunt switch. The HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> dielectric prepared in this work had the breakdown field higher than 20 MV/cm. The RF switch using 45-nm-thick HfO2 dielectric showed excellent performance. Its insertion loss is lower than 0.8 dB until 50 GHz at the up-state position. Its isolation is higher than 30 dB until 50 GHz at the down-state, particularly, higher than 50 dB in the range of 10 - 15 GHz

articleTitle: Distributed intelligent call admission control
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose QoS-based distributed intelligent call admission control (DICAC) for wideband multi-service CDMA system. Neural network is employed to predict next-step existing-call interference, fuzzy logic is used to estimate equivalent interference for a new call and make admission decision. QoS performances of all service types in home and neighboring cells are measured as feedback of the system. We introduce distributing idea into intelligent call admission control by defining the concept of equivalent dropping probability of neighboring cells. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can guarantee the QoS requirements of users, dropping probability and call blocking probability, in both home and neighboring cells.

articleTitle: A low complexity residual frequency offset compensation algorithm for coherent QPSK/16QAM OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the effects of residual frequency offset on OFDM systems are analyzed, and incorrect decision will be made due to the introduced signal constellation rotation. Kobayashi and Nikitopoulos present a method of estimating the phase rotation caused by residual frequency offset. In their work, phase error is obtained by comparing signals after frequency equalization with signals after decision, then compensates the following signals by using the estimated value of the phase rotation. The method involves two decision operations and the calculation of the quantity of every signal's phase rotation, consequently its computational complexity is high. Considering that in estimation what we need is only the phase information, we propose a method which obtains the phase rotation information from data directly by using such operations as sign inversion, real and imaginary part exchanging, accumulation and avoids two decision operations. The proposed method reduce the computational complexity without degrading the performance of the original algorithm, which is more suitable for hardware implementation. Simulation results show that the degradation of SNR caused by the residual frequency offset is not more than 0.2 dB after employing the proposed algorithm on the AWGN or SUI-2 channel.

articleTitle: A novel space-time turbo coding modulation technique for fading channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel space-time turbo coding modulation technique is presented in this paper. At the encoder, information bits are encoded using a concatenated space-time turbo coder, and then coded symbols are modulated and assembled by a pre-defined function rather than punctured as in other schemes. It can achieve lower code rate (because it doesn't puncture the coded signals), get more coding gains and take advantage of both space and time diversity. Since its decoding need to calculate two extrinsic probabilities simultaneously, traditional log-map decoding algorithm fails to be used directly. An extended 2-dimensional Log-Map decoding algorithm is developed to decode the proposed scheme. Simulation results and theoretical analysis exhibit its excellent performance. Under the same conditions, the proposed scheme will bring about 12 dB gains at BER 1.0 e-5 over some other known schemes at quasi-static fading channels, and above 10 dB at BER 1.0 e-5 over time-varying fading channels.

articleTitle: An effective scattering analysis for conducting bodies at the interior resonances
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: It is well known that either the electric field integral equations or the magnetic field integral equations have been widely employed to analyze electromagnetic scattering of conducting bodies. At some discrete resonance frequencies, however, when E-field integral equations or H-field integral equations are applied to attack this problem, the solution to method-of-moments matrix will be nonunique or unstable. A new effective modal method, termed Inagaki mode method, is presented here to solve this problem. At the interior resonances, this modal method, based on electric field integral equations, is used to filter out resonance modes and therefore obtain the right scattering property. The modal method doesn't need any operation of matrix inversion and possesses the merits of clarity in concept and simplicity in computation. A good agreement is achieved between the calculated results and the results published in some literatures as given in an analytical analysis.

articleTitle: Array pattern synthesis for optimum directivity with constrained array efficiency and specified sidelobe level
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to optimize the directivity with the controlled array efficiency and desired sidelobe level, a new pattern synthesis method is presented in this paper. This method can be applied to arbitrary array geometries. The array efficiency is restricted to be higher than a given value by incorporating a quadratic inequality constraint on the weight vector, and the desired sidelobe level is achieved by implementing linear constraints through iteration. By optimizing the array directivity subject to array efficiency and sidelobe constraints, the highest possible directivity with controlled array efficiency and desired sidelobe level can be achieved. The simulation results of different arrays show that the proposed method is very effective and flexible.

articleTitle: A centralized power allocation algorithm for TDD CDMA system with smart antenna in a multi-cellular environment
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In TDD CDMA systems, uplink and downlink work at the same frequency, which causes interference between them. The interference in uplink and downlink connection is analyzed respectively within a time slot. Adaptive beamforming is used in uplink receiver beamforming. Beam-steering method is used to achieve downlink transmission beamforming for complexity in downlink. From the beamforming gain and path gain between transmitter and receiver, a normalized gain matrix is constructed. With this matrix we propose an optimum power allocation method that satisfies all users' SIR requirements at the minimum transmission power. The power allocation algorithm provides an estimate of the optimum performance of all power control schemes

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for calculating CBP in large-scale sharing resource networks
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The call blocking probability (CBP) is one of the major parameters imposed to describe the quality of service (QOS) in network, and it is widely used to every kinds of network for all customers. With the increasing of network scale, conventional Kaufman recursion method and convolution method are unavailable for data overflow problem in large-scale network. In order to accommodate to large-scale network, revised Kaufman method and revised convolution method introduce a scheme to avoid data overflow, but they have tedious computation time for high computation complexity. A fast algorithm for calculating CBP is proposed in this paper. In large-scale network, the fast algorithm avoids data overflow by introducing a pre-process scheme, and decreases computation complexity by FFT method. Numerical results show that the fast algorithm has reliable accuracy and high speed.

articleTitle: The simulation of temperature distribution in tumor tissue heated alternately with interstitial hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to heating tumor tissue uniformly for a long time, a novel alternately heating method using interstitial antenna made from peeling outer conductor with cable sleeve of a standard coaxial was developed, the process was as follows: durative heating firstly, then alternate between heating and pause. Finite difference time domain (FDTD) method and finite difference method (FDM) are used to calculate the electromagnetic field and analyze the temperature distribution in tumor tissue, respectively. The simulation results show that the long-time uniform hyperthermia was achieved using alternately heating. Uniform hyperthermia area and temperature can be controlled by adjusting antenna's input power and working duration

articleTitle: Spatial colored co-channel interference reduction schemes in MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Spatial colored co-channel interference reduction schemes which focus on the receiver algorithms are explored, performance enhancement can be seen by taking spatial correlation factor into consideration, and simulation results are presented to show the performance comparison in different situation

articleTitle: System simulations for navigation and radar applications based on sophisticated numerical hybrid scattering analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Classical and modern navigation, landing and radar systems rely on the radio transmission and reception. Relevant objects in the radiation field can harm the intended characteristics of these systems. Modern state-of-the-art simulations can predict in an increasing number of complicated cases the electrical performance in the presence of these objects. Countermeasures can be designed from this knowledge. This paper deals mainly with the "threat" (potentially in-acceptable distortions) by the forthcoming new large aircraft A380 on the widely spread ILS (Instrument Landing System; operating at 110/330 MHz) installed on every major airport. The related system simulations and the mathematical and numerical analyses are outlined and some results for different numerical cases are presented. It is in particular emphasized to apply three-dimensional and sophisticated state-of-the-art methods, which are adapted to the three-dimensional characteristics of the objects in contrast to inadequately simple methods. For the case of the new Airbus A380, some principle results are presented using simple physical optics based methods, trials to improve the simple PO by creating "fudge factors" by measurements and in contrast results for rigorous and quasi-rigorous numerical methods. Large errors for a simple physical optics PO treatment in contrast to the rigorous method-of-moments MoM and improved physical optics IPO solution are presented and explained. The practical consequences for airports illustrate the necessity of reliable state-of-the-art system simulations and the application of advanced electromagnetic scattering analysis

articleTitle: Effect of element radiation patterns on the capacity of MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The concept of MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) has been for some time a topic of interest in the research community, since multiple antenna transmission allows a significant increase in the capacity of communication systems without requiring an increase in bandwidth or transmitting power. In this promising area there has been much attention given to system aspects such as space-time coding and decoding and channel modeling another vital area is the MIMO antenna arrays themselves. Currently, there are some major challenges, such as reducing the size of the array for small handsets while reducing the correlation between antenna elements. In this paper, we will discuss the effect of element radiation pattern in the antenna array on MIMO capacity. Both omni-directional and directive antennas are considered to provide a fair comparison, and furthermore, a specific type of antenna known as 'half-bowtie' is implemented in an array, being measured and simulated in given channel scenarios. The results illustrate that the more pattern diverse the elements are, the higher the mean capacity is, but also with the larger variance.

articleTitle: Effects of the earth to the electromagnetic field produced by broadcasting and television emission towers
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The purpose of his article is to provide the calculating formula of the electromagnetic field generated by the horizontal polarized broadcasting television transmitting antenna in space. The ground is considered as homogeneous, linear, and isotropic conducting medium. The space field strength is calculated through the sum of direct and reflected wave. Finally, a comparison is done between measured results and the calculated results using the formula taking the ground as ideal conductor a conducting medium and without considering the ground effect respectively. The advantage of the algorithmic is indicated by the analysis.

articleTitle: A novel approach of color interpolation for single image sensor
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Most digital imaging systems designers usually use a single CCD or CMOS image sensor with a color filter array (CFA) to acquire color image. In this paper, we are focusing on the development of a innovative interpolation method and its effective VLSI implementation of a low memory and low complexity architecture for Bayer CFA pattern. These features give it the potential to be used in consumer electronics and portable multimedia systems.

articleTitle: Ground electromagnetic smog estimation from airborne measurements: an effective approach
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new approach to find the electromagnetic field distribution on the ground from airplane surveys is proposed. The method exploits a temporal and spatial incoherent electromagnetic model of the radiation and an on board array antenna made of few elements. By solving a regularized ill-posed inverse problem, the technique allows the estimation of the on the ground intensity scene, taking explicitly into account the noise and the measurement errors due to the aircraft deviation from the nominal flight path and attitude of flight.

articleTitle: A PN code parallel acquisition algorithm for CDMA communication and its implementation on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel PN code parallel acquisition algorithm for CDMA communication is presented in the paper. Using the mapping methodology from algorithm to architecture, our algorithm is successfully implemented in FPGA chips to complement quick acquisition for PN code. Finally, the simulations results are presented for this algorithm.

articleTitle: Behavior of Berenger PML for absorbing TE/TM waves in rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The behavior of Berenger perfectly matched layer (PML) for absorbing nonTEM (TE & TM) waves in rectangular waveguide is analyzed in this paper. The attenuation constant and the phase constant of TE & TM waves in rectangular waveguide filling with Berenger PML are given. It is shown that Berenger PML can be used in finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation of rectangular waveguide operating at or near cutoff frequencies, due to the very small phase constant at these frequencies. A numerical example is given to show this.

articleTitle: A low-voltage RF amplifier using parallel triode MOSFET linearizing technique
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A low-voltage CMOS radio frequency amplifier using linearizing technique is presented in this paper. In this circuit, a parallel MOSFET in the triode region was used to boost the linearity. The circuit was fabricated with SMIC 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS process. Measurement shows that the input-referred 3rd-order intercept point (IIP/sub 3/) was improved by about 5 dB with little performances penalty.

articleTitle: Investigation of small dual-frequency spiral-like printed antennas for mobile communication
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a small dual-frequency printed antenna. The antenna is based on spiral-like shorted patch configuration with an additional shorting pin to generate the second resonance. The antenna resonance is at 1.55 GHz and 2.5 GHz. The performance of the new antenna is studied with its return loss and far-field radiation patterns presented here

articleTitle: Towards the era of ubiquitous networks
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk traces the evolution of wireless technologies from the early personal communications systems of the 1980's to the present day voice over IP and broadband multimedia services over the ubiquitous wireless network. The speaker will compare the parallel developments of wireless and wireline broadband networks and examine the extent of their convergence. Future trends in ubiquitous network technologies and some of the potential applications will also be discussed.

articleTitle: LAS-CDMA multi-code detection based on soft demodulation
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Next generation mobile communication networks appeal to data and multimedia communications, and require high efficiency and reliability. Multiple transmitting and multiple receiving BLAST system, advanced by Bell Laboratory, was combined with LAS-CDMA multiple access codes, possessing interference free windows IFW. This compound system will greatly increase parallel transportation channels and realize high-speed data transmission. In multi-cell networking circumstances, however, there exists severe inter-antenna interference and adjacent cell interference. To overcome the interferences, the receiver will combine uniform code joint detection with multi-code detection based on soft demodulation to divide the signals effectively. LAS-CDMA parallel transmitting system can realize large capacity and high reliability transportation in two-cell networking. It is an ideal solution for future mobile communication networks.

articleTitle: On the channel error count method with convolution code for adaptive transmission
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Channel error rate is an important performance measure of digital communication system. We usually use the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the decision statistic at the demodulator output to evaluate this quantity. For wireless transmission, the channel is time varying and highly random, hence an accurate channel error rate estimate at the demodulator output is hard to achieve. In order to maintain acceptable performance at the receiver end, adaptive transmission based on the instantaneous channel error rate is necessary. In this paper, we evaluate the effectiveness of a recently proposed channel error counts method to estimate the channel error rate used for adaptive transmission.

articleTitle: High-tension line data acquisition
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces the hardware and software of the high-tension line data acquisition system in detail. And the idea of the embedded system is applied to the design of it, in which /spl mu/C/OS-II-open source code real time multitask operation system is introduced. It is up to the high indexing both the data acquisition precision and the application convenience. The superior performance incarnates the embedded hardware building block design, multiple task real-time operating system and the programmable system.

articleTitle: Adaptive cyclostationary beamforming based on conjugate gradient algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This article proposes a complete adaptive GDB algorithm, based on conjugate gradient algorithm, which has been widely used in many real-time systems. Compared to GDB algorithm, it can provide faster convergence, which can be used in real-time systems. Further more, it doesn't need to modify any parameter, when input signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) has changed.

articleTitle: Calculation of the field distribution near electrically large surfaces with physical optics method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a new set of formulas to compute the field distribution near an electrically large conductor modeled by non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) surfaces using physical optics (PO) method. Results obtained by these formulas and by traditional PO method using triangle modeling technique agree well, which show the accuracy and efficiency of the formulations.

articleTitle: Modified equilateral triangular microstrip antenna (MT-MSA) with folded slots having constant intervals
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A fractal model for a planar antenna has been widely investigated as an effective antenna for achieving multi-band performance.
