publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes the system theory, performance and characteristic of a new developed FM multiplex data system (FMDS). The urban traffic integrated information real-time service system based on the new FM multiplex data system has also been designed.

Author Keywords: urban traffic integrated information real-time service system

articleTitle: EMC strategy in 340 MHz RF transceiver design
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: EMC is more and more important to RF circuits and system. However, some designers pay much attention to theory design but little to EMC. So there are some questions about EMC in designed circuits. This paper introduces some EMC application in 340 MHz RF (radio-frequency) transceiver.

articleTitle: A PC-based radar system simulator
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Computer-based radar simulators are largely used in radar signal analysis and processing. This contribution treats the simulation of pulsed Doppler radar system by using PC. The simulator has been implemented through hardware represented in an AT computer interface card while the software was build with C++ language. Samples of the simulated signals and screens are shown.

articleTitle: Transmit diversity schemes for WCDMA wireless communication system and their performance analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Transmit diversity scheme is a technique which can repel channel fading and improve system capacity effectively. It has been widely adopted in 3G wireless communication systems. The paper introduces several transmit diversity schemes which are used in WCDMA system. It presents their system models and arithmetics, gives their performance analysis, simulation and the conclusion.

articleTitle: Modal-based analysis of depth influence on SAR applied to the correlation study between averaged SAR and total dissipated power
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Measurement campaigns have shown that the electric field due to a mobile handset in an homogeneous phantom globally decays exponentially with depth. The aim of this paper is to clarify this behavior, which is the basis of some fast SAR assessment techniques, so as to specify the relationship between total dissipated power in a phantom and SAR averaged in a given cube of liquid. To this purpose, a 2-D modal analysis of power absorption in cylindrical and flat phantoms is first presented. This analysis is extended to the 3-D case of a GSM mobile phone close to a flat phantom, by means of a simplified field modal expansion as well as numerical calculation

articleTitle: 2-D DOA estimation in the presence of Gaussian noise with quaternion
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, quaternion was introduced in estimating azimuth and elevation of two dimensional direction of arrival (2-D DOA). We proposed a new quaternion signal model instead of classical complex signal model. Then, two definitions of multiplicative rules of quaternion were introduced. At last, we drew out azimuth and elevation using two definitions of quaternion and isomorphic complex expression of Hamilton's quaternion. Some simulations illustrated this new idea.

articleTitle: Adaptive modulated MIMO-OFDM for ultra wideband channel
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The development of ultra wideband (UWB) communications Is impeded by the drastic transmitted power limitations imposed by regulation authorities due to the "polluting" nature of these radio emissions with respect to existing services. In this work, uncoded adaptive modulated MIMO-OFDM benefit from both multiple transmit/receive antenna diversity order and exploiting the multipath diversity of the UWB channel It is used to enhance the link robustness through transmitting more information over subcarriers with better SNR. Simulations using modified S-V channel model indicates high system performance compared to conventional UWB-OFDM.

articleTitle: A robust efficient overlay multicast protocol for mobile ad hoc network
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Because of its relative simplicity and low overhead, overlay multicasting for MANET has been widely explored all over the world. By now, many overlay multicast protocols for MANET has been proposed. But most of these protocols aim only at improving the efficiency and ignore the dynamic and unreliable nature of MANET. Their performance usually degrades when these protocols are put into practice. In this paper, we propose a new overlay multicasting protocol, AREMP. In our protocol, we take full consideration of the dynamic nature of the network and try to improve both the reliability and the efficiency. Our simulation shows that our protocol can get a good balance between reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: An FPGA implementation of a structured irregular LDPC decoder
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a code construction method of irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is presented, which facilitates the hardware implementation of belief propagation (BP) decoders and leads to low error floors as well. To verify the effectiveness of this construction, an FPGA-based decoder is designed and implemented, where a novel non-uniform quantization scheme for BP decoding is used, so that the performance loss compared to infinite-precision decoding is less than 0.1 dB. The decoding throughput of the decoder can reach as high as 50 Mbps.

articleTitle: The algorithm and system architecture for high resolution real-time spaceborne SAR
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a refined chirp scaling algorithm for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging is presented. At first, the model of spaceborne SAR is analyzed. Based on the squint range model, a refined chirp scaling algorithm is derived. And it is suitable for precise imaging of high resolution spaceborne SAR with large range cell migration. Based on the refined chirp scaling algorithm, the system architecture is presented.

articleTitle: Theoretical implementation of antenna polarization to improve the reduction of co-channel interference in mobile cellular systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a new practical theory implementing antenna polarization to improve the co-channel interference reduction in mobile cellular systems such that when this approach is combined with the already existing reduction methods, the interference reduction degree will improve for the better

articleTitle: A design of new twin TEM cells
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new twin TEM cells' design is brought forward by analyzing symmetrical TEM Cells. This kind of twin TEM cells could doubly amplify the testing space. This paper analyzes electromagnetic field in the twin TEM cells using FEM method and draws a conclusion.

articleTitle: Multiband artificial magnetic conductors using stacked microstrip patch layers
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A two-dimensional microstrip patch array with a conducting via connecting the center of each patch to ground has been proposed for an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC). On the other hand, a microstrip patch array without vias has been shown to produce an AMC. This paper analyzes AMC structures with and without vias by using an effective medium model and finite difference time domain (FDTD) full-wave analysis method. The difference between the properties of these AMC structures is investigated in detail. Based on the results, we devised a multiband AMC structure having stacked microstrip patch layers. FDTD calculations and measurements were performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the multiband AMC.

articleTitle: A source routing algorithm for LEO satellite networks
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: One research challenge in low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks is to develop specialized and efficient routing algorithms. Based on datagram routing algorithm (DRA), a new routing algorithm, namely source routing algorithm (SRA), for LEO satellite networks is presented. Compared with DRA, it reduces computation overhead greatly while keeping the same overall performance. By the algorithm, the path with minimum propagation delay is discovered at the source satellite and stored in packet header, and then the packet is forwarded to its destination by intermediate nodes according to the path. Finally, the algorithm performance is evaluated through simulation and its computation complexity is analyzed to validate the efficiency of SRA.

articleTitle: MC-CDMA multiple-input multiple-output systems with space-time block codes
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we study the blind channel estimation and multiuser detection for quasi-synchronous MC-CDMA MIMO system with space-time block codes (STBC). Considering the Alamout's STBC scheme that involves two transmit antennas and multiple receive antennas, a sub space-based blind channel estimation for the STBC MC-CDMA system is proposed. Based on the first order perturbation theory, the mean-square error (MSE) of the channel estimation is derived. The weight analysis is obtained such that half of computational cost is reduced. Besides, both the forward backward averaging technique and the eigenspace technique are presented to enhance the performance of multiuser detection Finally, numerical simulations are given to evaluate and compare the proposed channel estimation and symbol detection techniques.

articleTitle: On the design of optimum subband filters for decision feedback generalized sidelobe canceller
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a decision feedback subband generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC), in which the design of the statistically optimum filter bank decomposition of the signals passing through the lower branch of the GSC as well as the signal after the decision feedback based on the minimum mean-square error criterion is addressed. The new beamformer not only renders superior interference cancellation capability, but also possesses a fast convergence rate due to the subband processing scheme and removal of the desired signal subband component in the output of the GSC via the decision feedback. Furthermore, to mitigate the computational overhead in the determination of the subband filter coefficients, an iterative procedure is also addressed. The convergence behavior of the new beamformer is conducted as well to justify the rationale of the new approach. Simulations are furnished to verity the superiority of the new beamformer.

articleTitle: Difference RCS of electromagnetic scattering from the target above a randomly rough surface
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The difference field RCS (d-RCS) has been defined to analyze the scattering from the target above a rough surface, which takes account of the scattering from the target and multiple interactions of the target and underlying rough surface. The d-RCS removes the effect of the finite illuminated surface length, under the tapered wave incidence. In this paper, our newly fast iterative approach is briefly reported. The electric field integral equations (EFIE) of the difference induced current oil the rough surface and the induced current oil the target are derived. An iterative approach is developed to solving the two EFIEs and scattering from both the target and underlying surface. How to choose the illuminated length of the rough surface for numerical iterations is discussed. Using the Monte Carlo method to realize the ocean-like rough surface, bistatic scatterings from the target, e.g. a cylinder or a square column, above a P-M (Pierson-Morkowitz spectrum) rough oceanic surface are numerically simulated for TE tapered wave incidence.

articleTitle: IEEE 802.15.4 compliant RF module design
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The RF module is designed using the CC2420 IC and ATmega128 MCU. The RF module, which is few in power consumer and small in size, works at the frequency of 2.4 GHz and is IEEE 802.15.4 compliant, and can be used widely in low-data-rate communications.

articleTitle: RCS calculation of a frequency band at arbitrary incidence angles and the components of aircraft using GRECO
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: GRECO method is regarded as one of the most effective method for high frequency approximation RCS calculation. It has many advantages such as little storage, fast speed and the calculation complexity not varying with the complexity and dimension of target. It is employed in this paper to calculate the RCS of a frequency band at arbitrary incidence angles quickly with a good precision by adjusting the view area within the screen automatically. In RCS reduction, we need to get the RCS contribution of components to the whole target. In this paper, the RCS contribution of the components to the whole target is also calculated which eliminates the shadow area from other components by hardware.

articleTitle: Effects of solar radiation on satellite antenna
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper is mainly about the effects on the satellite antenna performance of solar radiation. Polar orbit satellite works in the environment with frequent temperature change, its surface temperature varies significantly. This is mainly because the difference of solar radiation influence during its course. That means antennas that fixed on surface plate of the satellite have to endure such temperature variation. Normally, antenna is made of metal material with good conduction performance, which will change its shape with temperature variation. So, it is necessary to analyze the response of antenna to the environmental temperature change.

articleTitle: Trace termination design
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we study several termination methods in PCB trace design. Trace termination plays an important role in ensuring optimal signal integrity as well as minimizing creation of RF energy. Termination may be required to prevent trace impedance problems and provide higher quality signal transfer between circuits.

articleTitle: A modified UTD model for indoor propagation prediction
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a modified UTD model to predict the propagation channel parameters in indoor scenarios is presented. The model is based on the blueprint of the rooms for a transmitter and receiver located at the same room. It employs two plane views reference to the transmitter and the receiver, respectively and a new criteria adopting vector's dot product to construct the visibility graph. To verify the model, comparisons between the simulation results and measurements available in literature are given. The numerical results show that the modified ray tracing model will be applied in complex indoor propagation environment and find all propagation paths from a transmitter to a receiver in a high degree of accuracy without redundant computation time.

articleTitle: Radiation field calculation of Luneburg lens antenna using reciprocity theory
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Study is made on the scattering problem of a plane wave incident on a stepped-index Luneburg lens. Then, the radiation field of the stepped-index Luneburg lens antenna (LLA) is obtained by the use of coordinate transformations and reciprocity theory. Finally, some curves useful for the design of the LLA feed are plotted

articleTitle: SiGe power HBTs and MMIC medium power amplifiers operated at 8-10 GHz
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we report the first performance characteristics of SiGe power HBTs and medium power MMIC power amplifiers operating at 8-10 GHz. SiGe power HBTs have been demonstrated using properly designed device structure and employing a proper operation configuration. It is illustrated that a box-type Ge profile with high Ge content can allow a high base doping level while still maintaining high breakdown voltages and without using submicron emitter stripes. The high doping level dramatically improves the power gain values of SiGe HBTs and makes the CB configuration more favorable for power amplification than CE configuration. High power performance has thus been achieved from SiGe HBTs at 8 and 10 GHz. Single-stage medium power amplifiers operating at 8 GHz has also been demonstrated using these SiGe HBTs.

articleTitle: Estimating frequencies of two dimensional harmonics with extended quaternion matrix pencil
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel algorithm to estimate frequency pairs of two dimensional harmonics, whose frequency pairs might share the common frequency. First, we presented a new math model of two dimensional harmonics signal, which was based on quaternion. Then, we presented operation rules definitions of Hamilton's quaternion and Ma's quaternion. After analyzing the properties of two kind of quaternion, we computed correlation function of quaternion data model using Ma's operation rules and constructed extended quaternion matrix of correlation function data. At last, we proposed our estimation method using Hamilton's operation rules. Some simulations illustrated our idea.

articleTitle: Conical coupled stripline transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new structure is proposed to use as an interconnect in the VLSI circuits. This structure has a shield and some strip lines all in conical form. After describing the full-wave formulation, the approximate transmission-line analysis of the structure is presented. The properties of the structure are studied using an example.

articleTitle: 3-dimensions analytical modeling of the optical carriers injection in a semiconductor substrate
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to be faster and more precise than numerical way in the computation of the photo-induced plasma in semiconductor, we have to use an analytical approach to solve the problem. In this study, we use the Hankel transform to simplify the resolution of the differential equation of second order with non-constant coefficient, known as the diffusion equations. As a result, we obtain the 3-dimensions carrier density based on all the physical parameters of the substrate and of the laser beam and so we are able to study the sensibility to several parameters.

articleTitle: Research on a novel sleeve antenna and its applications
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A sleeve antenna mounted on metallic cylinder is analyzed by moment method. The electric characteristic parameters of this novel sleeve antenna are calculated, including the input impedance, the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR), the horizontal gain and radiation pattern. Finally, a pair of practical antennas are designed, working in the 105 ~ 420 MHz and 225 ~ 600 MHz frequency band respectively. The calculated results are in good agreement with the experimental results

articleTitle: Robust blind adaptive beamforming for cyclostationary signals
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of robust adaptive array beamforming for cyclostationary signals. By exploiting the signal cyclostationarity, blind adaptive beamforming algorithms have found numerous important applications in signal processing. However, these methods suffer from severe performance degradation even if there is a small mismatch in the cycle frequency of the desired signal. In this paper, we propose the efficient robust scheme based on the conventional cyclic adaptive beamforming (CAB) algorithm against the mismatch in the cycle frequency. The performance of the proposed techniques is compared with that of existing blind cyclic beamforming approaches by simulation examples, the results of which demonstrate a marked improvement in the robustness against imprecisely knowledge of the cycle frequency

articleTitle: Performance of space-time block-coded multicarrier DS-CDMA system in a multipath fading channel
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a space-time block-coded (STBC) multicarrier direct-sequence code-division multiple access (MC-DS-CDMA) system is proposed. The performance of the system is theoretically analyzed in a multipath fading channel and the corresponding BER expressions are derived, which is verified through simulations. Numerical results show that better performance with the proposed system is achieved than that of conventional MC-DS-CDMA system

articleTitle: Bounded Brownian bridge model for UWB indoor multipath channel
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Regarding a transmitter and a receiver as two fixed points of the Brownian bridge process, an ultra-wideband (UWB) multipath as a trajectory of the Brownian bridge process, all reflection points of paths situating on the surfaces of obstacles, and adopting two-value phase assumption, a bounded Brownian bridge model (BBBM) for UWB indoor multipath channel is constructed. Using BBBM to simulate a corridor environment of two glass doors with a metal grid inside, several characteristic parameters of UWB channel are obtained. The power delay profiles (PDPs) are similar to the results from other experiments

articleTitle: A DSSS receiver for dual-mode DSSS/OFDM wireless LAN systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a DSSS baseband receiver suitable for a dual mode DSSS/OFDM wireless LAN system. Packet synchroniser with a pair of ADCs with dynamic sampling is used for detecting both DSSS and OFDM packets. For differentially encoded symbols, frequency offset and phase offset can be compensated based on their inherent characteristics. For high data rate DSSS based modulations, channel estimation and equalization with receive diversity combining in frequency domain is applied to resolve the multipath distortions. With channel equalization and diversity combining of the DSSS receiver achieved in frequency domain the overall complexity of the dual mode DSSS/OFDM equalization can be realized.

articleTitle: Absorbing properties of the magnetic composite electromagnetic wave absorber
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22.4</sub>O <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</sub> hexagonal ferrite was obtained by conventional ceramic technology. Fe-5wt%Ni alloy was also prepared by mechanical alloying method. Electromagnetic (EM) characteristics of the two materials were measured in a frequency range of 2-18 GHz. The absorption performances of metal-backed single-layered coating and double-layered coating were numerically simulated. Results show that preferable properties of EM absorption can be obtained by the double-layered design of ferrite and Fe-Ni alloy. The minimum reflection loss is -32.96 dB and the bandwidth of -10 dB is over 7 GHz at 3 mm. Thus, it is possible to make thinner broadband EM wave absorber by adjusting input impedance of the composite materials

articleTitle: Application studies of dielectric resonator antennas
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the properties of cylindrical and rectangular DRAs are reviewed and applications of the antennas to polarization control, polarization diversity, and direction of arrival determination are described. Theoretical and experimental results show that cylindrical and rectangular DRAs have useful radiation and impedance characteristics, which are determined by the permittivity of the dielectric material and dimensions of the resonator. It also shows that DRAs can be controlled to provide linearly or circularly polarized radiation, and they can be used in a diversity system, and the determination of DOA

articleTitle: Improved channel estimation algorithm for OFDM over LEO channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: For the study of OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing) system for LEO (Low Earth Orbits) satellite communication, a channel estimation algorithm by Kalman filtering based on comb-type pilot subcarriers is proposed in this paper. Due to the statistical characteristics of LEO channel, an OFDM system model on the frequency domain is derived and the correlation of the process noises in Kalman filtering between two consecutive identical signals at the same pilot subcarrier are modeled as the first Markov chain. The performance of the proposed method is compared with LS (Least Square) channel estimator by measuring bit error rate (BER) with QPSK, BPSK, 8-PSK and 16QAM as modulation schemes. The simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Wide-band frequency estimation with two different sub-Nyquist temporal sampling rates
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method is presented for wide-band frequency estimation with sub-Nyquist sampling by using two independent sampling channels at the different rates. With low cost of hardware and moderate computation, the proposed method is not sensitive to the relative amplitude and phase errors of both channels. Simulations demonstrate the capabilities of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on the real-time registration technique for radar networking
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Since the system errors degrade the association and fusion of the tracks from different radars greatly, registration is the vital problem for the data fusion of the radar network. But the measurements are always nonlinear function of the system biases; therefore, Kalman filter is unable to be used directly two methods are proposed in this paper to solve this problem. First, we use the linear model of literature (M.P Dana, 1990), and present an extended Kalman filter. Second, a sequential Monte Carlo approach is applied to real-time estimation of the state and the system errors, this method is known as particle filtering (M.Sanjeev Arumpalam et al., 2002) also. In the end, simulation results show the effectiveness of the two methods.

articleTitle: Indoor propagation loss in 70 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, measurement procedures of propagation loss and examination results between propagation loss and distance in 70 GHz band are reported For the propagation loss, differences of approximate equations in the various environments, such as LoS and NLoS, and relation between an antenna beam width and an attenuation coefficient for distance are discussed

articleTitle: Improvement in SOVA based normalization scheme for turbo codes
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Normalizing the soft output of SOVA is commonly used to improve the performance of SOVA. Normalization based on the fixed sealing factor is a simple and effective strategy. In this paper, we investigate the applicability of the fixed scaling factor to the BR-SOVA (SOVA proposed by Battail). In the proposed scheme, the soft output of BR-SOVA is normalized by the fixed scaling factor. The performance of proposed techniques is studied through simulation. The simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme results in improvement in performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of circular antenna arrays with MRC in Nakagami fading channels by approximate approaches
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Multiple antenna systems are promising architectures for overcoming the effects of multi-path interference and increasing the spectrum efficiency. Spatial correlation among antenna elements, due to limited angular spread or insufficient antenna spacing, significantly reduces the performance of the diversity reception systems. In this paper, we explore the performance for circular antenna arrays with MRC (maximal ratio combining) in Nakagami fading channels by exact and approximate approaches. By including spatial information, we derive spatial correlation functions of circular antenna arrays. Analytical formulas of average bit error ratio (BER) are also derived as a function of covariance matrix of the multi-path signals. The effects of antenna configurations and the wireless environment are illustrated.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s CMOS limiting amplifier for optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A 10 Gb/s limiting amplifier for fiber-optic transmission system is realized in a 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS technology, the whole circuit consists of an input-buffer network, four gain cells, and a output buffer for driving 50 /spl Omega/ transmission lines and offset compensation for offset cancellation. This limiting amplifier allows an input dynamic is rang of 32 dB (20mV-800 mV) and provides a constant output voltage swing (800 mV/sub pp/), the power dissipation is 99 mW with the supply voltage of 3.3 V, the chip area is 0.8/spl times/1.3 mm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: Adaptability between FM-DCSK and channel coding over fading channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: FM-DCSK is a non-coherent modulation and demodulation technique that uses chaotic signals as the carrier. Due to its inherent broadband nature, its good performance of anti-multipath-fading is promising for wireless communications. In order to improve the global performance of such chaotic communication systems, enhanced FM-DCSK based on the Woven convolutional code (WCC) is presented. Through system simulations, this article demonstrates that the WCC-based FM-DCSK system is superior to that of the traditional code-based FM-DCSK system and the original FM-DCSK system over AWGN, Rayleigh and Ricean flat fading channels, especially with prominent coding gains over fading channels. It is further verified that there exists adaptability between FM-DCSK and channel coding. This finding will be significant for optimizing and analyzing the performance of the FM-DCSK system improved by good channel coding schemes, towards better applications of the chaotic communication technology in the future.

articleTitle: Ludwig algorithm's improvement and its application on NURBS-PO method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, Ludwig's algorithm is improved to compute the target's radar cross section (RCS). The target is modeled with non uniform rational Bezier surface (NURBS), so the integral needed to be calculated is different to that based on triangle facets. The author modified Ludwig's algorithm to evaluate the integral, the result in this paper shows that the new formula is valid.

articleTitle: On the performance of LDPC coded MC-CDMA in Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate the performance of LDPC coded MC-CDMA in Rayleigh fading channels. We derive an exact expression of the variance of multiuser interference and obtain the optimal maximum number of iterations in LDPC decoding. Compared to turbo coded MC-CDMA, the LDPC coded MC-CDMA has advantages in BER performance and complexity. The simulation results also show that the system using MMSEC outperforms the system using MRC in BER performance and complexity.

articleTitle: Investigation on traffic modeling and its applications in wireless communication simulations
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The growing portion of packet data traffic in mobile communication systems makes it important that accurate traffic models for various services be obtained for network planning and provisioning. In this paper, we present traffic models for typical mobile data services including VoIP, video, WWW and FTP to assist in the evaluation and engineering of data services in mobile communication systems. We also discuss how to adjust related traffic model parameters to facilitate simulations.

articleTitle: Challenges and strategies of the spectrum management
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This article describes the changes in spectrum management, driven by modern communications system concepts and new-type RF hardware and software developments, briefly discusses strategy of the spectrum management in the future, including spectrum-sharing technology, multi-dimension frequency assignments, and dynamically allocated frequency assignments spectrum concept. This article draws the following conclusion in sum: 1) new-type RF technology and broadband signal are being used extensively, and the frequency band suitable for mobile communication has been already very crowded. 2) The objective actuality request the frequency management spectrum organization must adopt the counter measure, changing the traditional frequency spectrum management. 3) New-type broadband system application of technology frequently, already or will soon become the main reason that system appears electromagnetic compatible problem.

articleTitle: A research on the negative delay circuit in application to signal sampling and processing systems
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method using negative delay circuit to cancel out the positive group delays due to "transistor latency" in signal sampling and processing systems is proposed in this paper. Using the negative group delay circuit, the advance time more than twenty percent of the input pulse width can be easily be achieved. The underlying principle of the method is that negative feedback can be used to produce negative group delays. It is easily to see that the application of the negative group delay circuit can speed up the communication systems, and the new method proposed in this paper may be widely used in microelectronic communication domain.

articleTitle: A cross-entropy based parameter for ship detection from a polarimetric SAR image
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A cross-entropy based parameter is proposed to measure the difference between a river area and others. This parameter can be employed for ship detection from a polarimetric SAR image. After deciding the boundaries of the river area, ships are detected only in the river area instead of the whole site. Therefore, most of the false alarms are eliminated. Finally, the performance of this new approach is validated by the X-band full polarimetric SAR data in Niigata area of Japan.

articleTitle: Influences of EUT with different properties on the performances of a reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: It is studied in detail that the influences of EUT with different properties on the reverberation chamber performances. Different amounts of absorbers have been added to load the chamber. It is found suitable amount of load may increase the chamber performance but more absorbers may decrease it. The influences of metal EUT on performance of a chamber have been studied by placing different size of metal enclosure in chamber. It is found a big size metal EUT deteriorate the performance though the load is small.

articleTitle: Near-field analysis of airborne antenna array by the UTD method
publicationTitle: 2005 IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A near-field model of antenna array which is combined with the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) is presented to analyze the near-field and far-field of an airborne antennas array. Approximate model of the airplane structure is employed to obtain the computed field. A major feature of this analysis is that when the receiver exists in the near field of the array it can be considered in the far field of each element of the array because of the tiny size of the element. Furthermore, the UTD is very suitable to compute the electrically large structure such as an airplane. The analysis of both the near and far field of an airborne ellipse planar array has been made in this paper, and the results have been obtained This model can be widely used in the EMC prediction for antenna array system in a complex environment.
